segments: The Romans, however, did not accept [the terms];
and at the dawn of the Sunday of Unleavened Bread, they prepared for battle.
And it was a cold day,
and the wind was against the Romans.
And they appeared weak and fled;
and many were killed {OCR: ܐܸܬ݂ܩܲܛܲܠܘ};
and the rest fell {OCR: ܢܦܲܠܘ} into the Euphrates and were drowned.
Concerning this Justinian, John of Amida [John of Asia] relates:
"For thirty years I was in his association,
and I never saw that he ceased from building churches.
For ninety-six churches,
and twelve monasteries, and xenodocheia (hospices?):
he said,
that through my hands he built in the regions of Asia, Caria, Phrygia, and Lydia."
And in his fourth year, Khosrow son of Kavadh reigned over the Persians for forty-seven years.
And there was peace between the Romans and the Persians for seven years.
And the Samaritans in Palestine appointed for themselves a leader,
and entered Neapolis,
and killed the bishop and many people,
and plundered and burned many temples.
And the Romans marched up and subdued the city,
and killed {OCR: ܘܲܩܛܲܠܘ} their leader and the majority of them.
Then Domnus (Gelimer?) rebelled in Carthage;
and Belisarius went and subdued him and brought the tyrant {OCR: ܠܛܲܪܘܼܢܵܐ} in chains.
And in the eleventh year of Justinian, the peace between the Persians and the Romans was dissolved.
And a comet (great and fearful) was seen in the evening time for many days.
And in that same year, Khosrow marched up and took captive Antioch, Aleppo, and Apamea in a bitter captivity.
And the Romans also went down to Persia,
and took captive the country of the Kurds, of the Arzanenes, and of the Arabs.
And again Khosrow marched up and took captive Callinicum and all of Mesopotamia.
And again he marched up against Edessa;
and when he was not able to conquer it,
he took Batnan captive and departed.
And again he marched up against Antioch and conquered it,
and burned it,
and exiled it completely.
And the Persians took {OCR: ܘܲܫܩܲܠܘ} even the marble slabs that were on the walls,
and took them down to Persia.
And again the Persians marched up and plundered the whole region of the Limites (the borders?),
and laid waste Callinicum and Beth Balash,
and took {OCR: ܘܲܫܩܲܠܘ} the bones of Mor Bacchus the martyr, and the gold that was on the sarcophagus of Mor Sergius.
And in the year 848 [of the Greeks],
(537 of our Lord?), there was a sign in the sun, the like of which had never been seen before.
